Name: Mandatum
Description:
Sustainable DiscountsTM by Mandatum generates reliable, recurrent, and sustainable funding to protect forests and oceans in the Global South by unlocking trillions of dollars trapped in market inefficiencies — addressing climate change and the biodiversity crisis while advancing environmental justice. 

Mandatum is a breakthrough funding engine that redirects a portion of the $2 trillion consumers unknowingly overpay each year in retail markups—unlocking hundreds of billions annually for nature conservation, without asking anyone to spend more.

We don’t rely on government pledges, carbon markets, or voluntary donations—all of which have repeatedly failed to close the $950 billion annual nature funding gap. This shortfall is not just a financial problem—it is arguably the world’s most urgent environmental challenge, and it threatens to undermine all other climate progress. Without sustainable funding, no climate or biodiversity goal—no matter how well-designed—can succeed.

SDTM tackles the root issue: affordability. Using our “Sustainable DiscountsTM,” we empower people and businesses to support conservation while shopping—redirecting a portion of existing consumer spending into forest and ocean protection at no extra cost. It’s not a donation. It’s a redirection that transforms consumption into climate justice: the more people shop, the more they help restore ecosystems and support the communities who depend on them. And because shopping is a constant in our economy, the solution scales naturally across all forms of commerce—not just online.
Why does this matter? Because when we stop the destruction of nature, we also fight poverty, hunger, water scarcity, disease, and economic instability. Forests and oceans directly support 1.2 billion people, and nature loss is the third largest source of CO2 emissions globally—if it were a country, it would outrank every nation but China and the U.S.

Amoretti Limited is building FungiOS, the world's first AI-powered platform to harness the untapped potential of the fungal kingdom. We are redefining humanity's relationship with fungi, transforming industries from health and agriculture to defense and materials.

At Amoretti Limited, we believe the future is fungal. For centuries, fungi have been misunderstood, often relegated to the botanical realm. Yet, genetically, they are closer to animals, operating through intricate, intelligent mycelial networks that hold secrets to unprecedented innovation.

We are the pioneers behind FungiOS, a revolutionary AI-driven platform that acts as the central nervous system for the fungal kingdom. FungiOS leverages advanced Large Mycelial Models (LMMs) to analyze vast, multi-modal datasets – from genomic sequences and biochemical profiles to environmental parameters and growth kinetics. This deep intelligence allows us to predict optimal growth conditions, discover novel compounds, and engineer fungal systems with unparalleled precision.

Our mission is to unlock the immense, untapped potential of fungi across three transformative verticals:

Amoretti Health: Optimizing the biosynthesis of therapeutic compounds (e.g., psilocybin, lion's mane) for pharmaceutical and wellness applications, accelerating drug discovery, and enabling personalized fungal medicine.

Amoretti Enterprise: Revolutionizing agriculture with programmable food, scaling sustainable biomaterials (e.g., mycelium leather, packaging), and enhancing industrial processes through fungal biotechnology.

Amoretti Defense: Mapping toxic fungal compounds for biodefense applications, developing rapid detection methods, and contributing to national security through advanced mycological intelligence.

FungiOS is more than a platform; it's a self-reinforcing ecosystem. As more data flows in from diverse sources – researchers, farmers, hobbyists, and sensors – our LMMs become exponentially smarter, generating new insight.

Engineered by a research team and validated through significant testing since 2019, Oreqa is tested in 120°F Arizona summers, on weak feeder nodes, in high-consumption homes, and adjacent to AI datacenters. It is engineered to perform anywhere, under any conditions.

What Oreqa provides
—	Full-home electrical service, around the clock, every day of the year.
—	Continuous operation through outages — every circuit, no switching delay, no homeowner action.
—	Insulation from utility rate volatility for the life of the agreement.

Description:

ORSS deploys advanced systems, including Oceanic Restoration Submersive Systems (ORSS) and Oceanic Restoration Cooling Systems (ORCS), to restore coral reefs, support marine biodiversity, mitigate hurricane intensity, and filter pollutants like microplastics. With initial deployments in Malibu, the Great Barrier Reef, and India, the project aims to scale globally, revitalizing ecosystems and protecting vulnerable coastal communities.

The project’s impact extends beyond environmental restoration. Through eco-tourism packages, sustainable fisheries revenue, regional licensing, carbon credits, and data monetization, ORSS generates diversified income streams while supporting local economies and creating jobs. Key innovations include AI-powered monitoring stations for real-time biodiversity tracking, Coral Reef Restoration Facilities (CRRFs) to double coral reef footprints in 30 years, and renewable energy systems integrated into ORSS units. Together, these advancements turn marine conservation into a scalable, profitable global industry.

By restoring ecosystems, reducing climate risks, and supporting global food security, the ORSS Project demonstrates that environmental sustainability and economic resilience can go hand in hand. Join us in transforming ocean restoration and creating a sustainable legacy for future generations.

Batteries are at the heart of the energy transition and digital transformation, powering AI, data centers, e-mobility, robotics, and autonomous systems. However, as the industry faces dire industrialization challenges, innovation is key to overcoming this hurdle.

As Steve Blank famously said, "Startups don't fail because they lack a product; they fail because they lack customers and a profitable business model." The Battery Saloon partners with startups to lead them from lab to gigafactories, functioning as a fractional product manager, and leveraging our robust network of highly technical industry leaders, national labs and academic institutions, investors, and service providers. What sets us apart is our focus and deep technical expertise. The built environment already consumes 50% of all extracted natural resources while accounting for one-third of industrial emissions, driving climate change, ecosystem destruction, and sand & gravel depletion two to three times faster than natural renewal. Sand mining destroys river ecosystems, collapses deltas, and fuels violent illegal mining.

At the same time, global plastic and industrial waste is surging — with billions of tons of material landfilled or incinerated and total waste volumes expected to double by 2050 — fueling a worldwide waste crisis.

MAA’VATM develops regenerative, circular, carbon‐negative concrete materials from recycled plastic and manufacturing waste — turning materials destined for landfill or incineration into high‐performance, lightweight, CO2‐sequestering concrete aggregates that reduce water demand and advance solutions to river sand shortages, water scarcity, ecosystem collapse, climate change, and the global waste crisis simultaneously, addressing a $1T+ global aggregates market.

Name: Clema
Description:
Clema builds cooling systems for crews who work in heat and need to keep moving. Extreme heat already costs U.S. employers more than $100B a year in lost productivity, and >2B workers worldwide face rising temperatures on the job. Across warehouses, construction, energy, logistics, agriculture, and defense, heat slows output, drives fatigue and errors, and increases incident rates. In many facilities, productivity can drop 20–50 percent on hot days. Breaks, fans, and ice help, but they still pull people off-task and rarely last a full shift.

We design equipment for continuous performance. Our active-cooling wearables deliver steady cooling even in high humidity, run for 8–12 hours, and integrate with standard gear. Lightweight builds, balanced weight distribution, and sealed systems designed for dust, debris, and movement. No melting packs that fade after 60–90 minutes. No hoses or fans that get in the way. No reliance on trucks or tents that turn cooling into downtime.

Teams adopt Clema to:
• Maintain throughput during heat waves and peak season surges
• Cut heat-related downtime and reduce incident risk
• Support retention in high-turnover, high-heat roles
• Prepare for tightening OSHA and insurer expectations

We test with the people who lift, weld, operate, harvest, and load every day. Their experience shapes fit, weight, airflow, runtime, and durability so cooling feels invisible and performance lasts from first hour to last.

Heat isn’t a seasonal nuisance anymore. It’s a daily operational constraint. Clema gives employers and workers a way to sustain pace, safety, and endurance when temperatures rise.

Name: NEXT TFX
Description:
NEXT TFX is pioneering the next generation of ultra-high-pressure reverse osmosis (UHPRO) membranes to transform how industries manage water and extract valuable resources. At the convergence of water scarcity and growing global demand for critical minerals, our technology provides a breakthrough solution that enables both clean water production and mineral recovery from the same membrane system.

Developed in partnership with co-founder and co-inventor Dr. Eric Hoek at UCLA's Samueli School of Engineering, our membrane platform uses a three-layer structure with a unique resin-based coating. This structure withstands ultra-high pressures, allowing operators to push filtration further than traditional reverse osmosis systems. Whether targeting desalination or brine concentration for rare earth element (REE) recovery, NEXT Membranes delivers double the performance at half the energy.

The challenge we address is urgent and growing. Lithium demand alone is projected to grow fivefold by 2035, driven by electric vehicle (EV) adoption and global energy transition goals. At the same time, desalination and water reuse are becoming essential in water-scarce regions. Conventional RO membranes are not equipped to handle the higher salinity, fouling, and pressure requirements of these modern demands. NEXT Membranes offers a new standard for membrane durability, efficiency, and versatility.

Our dual-market focus allows us to create significant commercial impact. On one side, we’re solving real pain points for lithium and mineral producers who need more efficient, higher-recovery brine concentration systems. On the other, we offer water utilities and government agencies a new tool to extend water supply and reduce waste byproduct volumes. In many cases, NEXT Membranes can do both simultaneously, making desalination more energy-efficient while recovering valuable minerals from the concentrate stream.

The core idea of Nemo's Garden is to create self-sustaining underwater greenhouses, leveraging the natural properties of seawater to enable the growth of plants and vegetables. These submerged pods harness the consistent temperatures found underwater, absence of pests, and an abundance of water to create an optimal growing environment. This approach not only addresses land-based agricultural limitations like drought, land degradation, and limited freshwater resources but also opens a new frontier in responsible use of ocean space.
Each biosphere in Nemo's Garden is a transparent, air-filled dome where crops are grown in a controlled environment. The plants are grown in hydroponic systems.
The project is not just about food production; it's a bold step towards sustainable and eco-compatible solutions. The underwater conditions eliminate the need for pesticides and herbicides, contributing to a cleaner and more organic form of agriculture.
In terms of commercialization, Nemo's Garden is not just a scientific experiment; it's a viable model for future food production. The initiative envisions these underwater pods not just as isolated experiments but as a network of sustainable food sources, potentially revolutionizing how we approach food scarcity and environmental sustainability. It's a vision of a future where humanity harmonizes technological advancement with ecological balance, tapping into the vast resources of our oceans in a responsible and innovative way.

The Fashion Industry is the second largest polluter, responsible for 10% of the global carbon emissions and 20% of the industrial waste water. Textile manufacturing is the most environmentally demanding part of the production process, attributing to 60% of the overall carbon and waste water. Even worse, as high as 15% of textiles produced are discarded (incinerated or put into landfill) due to (1) minimum order quantity requirements, (2) inaccurate demand forecasting, and (3) poor industry practices (cheaper to produce excess than a separate batch). The result is overproduced materials (aka pre-consumer, post-industrial waste) that sit in a suppliers' warehouses until room needs to be made for new production orders. Most of this waste is happening behind closed doors. The carbon footprint of a footwear or apparel item is actually more than that material used to create the item.

SproutGround’s mission is to bring waste due to overproduction to zero. We are creating a market for this excess material by sourcing materials from our network of Tier 2 suppliers (textile rolls). Brands benefit from providing more environmentally friendly practices/products at an affordable price, and at scale. Additionally, we guarantee no waste/excess by holding the material and not requiring a minimum order - brands can take what they need, when they need it. Lastly, the material lead time is significantly lower than made-to-order produced virgin material.

We plan to revolutionize the way these facilities use technology, to make them more streamlined, accurate, and profitable - which means more recyclables avoid the landfill, and more of our natural resources are protected.

For battery manufacturers, IonSight is the first inspection system built for in-line deployment at industrial speeds, enabling real-time, cell-by-cell feedback across formation, end-of-line, and beyond. By detecting defects the moment they occur—not weeks later—manufacturers can adopt a No Fault Forward process, drastically reducing scrap, rework, and the high cost of delayed quality corrections. IonSight detects what CT and electrical tests miss—before defects become recalls.

For EV and BESS integrators, IonSight offers a powerful new capability: the ability to verify cell quality before assembly, ensure cell balancing, and make data-driven supplier decisions—without destructive testing or slow sampling processes.

Titan’s mission is to enable safe, high-performing, and cost-effective batteries at scale. Whether at the heart of a gigafactory or validating incoming inventory for an integrator, IonSight gives every stakeholder the tools to eliminate faults, reduce risk, and optimize every cell—from the inside out.

Takachar develops small-scale, low-cost, and portable systems that can latch onto the back of tractors and pick-up trucks, and deploy to rural, hard-to-access communities to locally upgrade and densify residues on-site into higher-value, carbon-negative bioproducts such as fertilizer blends, biofuels, and chemicals. Our goal is to create a network of self-sufficient rural communities less dependent on unreliable imported supply chains for their essential chemical commodities. Name: Aircapture
Description:
Aircapture is creating a circular commercial carbon economy utilizing novel Direct Air Capture (DAC) technology. Our modular, on-site DAC machines capture CO2 from the atmosphere and make it immediate available for our customers' production processes. The result is a cheaper, cleaner and greener supply of CO2. 

Previously, commercially available CO2 was produced and distributed only in ways that generate large amounts of greenhouse gas emissions, result in product impurities and include the often-substantial friction costs from transportation.

For every tonne of delivered CO2, we estimate two or more tonnes of CO2 are emitted into the atmosphere, contributing to global warming and creating significant supply chain emissions, the cost of which are likely to materially increase.

Reducing greenhouse gas emissions alone is not enough to avoid catastrophic climate change. Atmospheric carbon dioxide removal addresses legacy emissions and drives the development of critical, sustainable carbon-negative infrastructure.

By utilizing atmospheric CO2, we can actually turn back the hands of time – reversing much of the damage that has already been done – while enabling our customers to economically build new carbon-to-value industries and alleviate energy poverty on a global scale.

Our mission is to use Direct Air Capture (DAC) to help achieve these goals. DAC can be sited practically anywhere. There are no natural or technical limits to its scale, the quantity of carbon dioxide it removes is verifiable and it is cost-effective today.

Biochar is one of the most proven, scalable, and durable carbon removal methods available today. It has delivered more verified carbon removal than any other durable method, with over 800,000 tonnes removed since 2022. By heating crop waste—like husks, shells, and prunings—at high temperatures without oxygen, biochar locks carbon away for centuries and creates credits that sell for far more than typical offsets.

Agribusinesses value biochar because it turns low-value waste into reliable revenue and improves soil health. Buyers value it because it’s verifiable, cost-effective, and available now. But despite the demand, supply still lags. High upfront costs, sourcing challenges, and complex carbon markets have slowed new producers from getting started.

Terraton exists to change that. We make biochar simple to start, profitable to run, and scalable across thousands of producers—so carbon removal can keep pace with what the climate demands.

CO2Rail Company is a US-based climate tech company that has developed proprietary rail-based, self-powered, dual-mode Direct Air Capture (DAC) and Locomotive Emissions Mitigation (CCS) technology which removes excess carbon dioxide from the ambient air or rail transportation point sources. The technology leverages the tremendous scale and scope of the global rail network, purpose-built rail equipment, and sustainable train-generated regenerative braking energy with no external energy inputs required. This will broadly enable rail as the first carbon-negative mode of heavy transport.

The CO2Rail DAC technology deploys specially designed, self-contained DAC railcars on both diesel and electrified rail lines outfitted with battery arrays, CO2 direct air capture systems, compression equipment, and ancillary gear that uniquely exploits the substantial sustainable energy generated on-board the train through regenerative braking. The units are equipped with large intakes that extend up into the slipstream of the moving train and collect CO2 feedstock air by fluidic, ramjet-type processes, places no demand on energy or land resources. At scale, CO2Rail will operate near 93% net LCA CO2 efficiency including the carbon debt incurred in transportation of the reclaimed CO2 to geological sequestration. Unloaded daily at crew change or fueling stops into regular CO2 tank cars, the network will curate delivery of the harvested CO2 to on-route sites for permanent underground sequestration, or delivery to end-users as feedstock for the circular carbon economy.

Name: Carbon.XTM
Description:
The "Emissions Race" has led to overly ambitious climate targets in too short a time-frame. It's a hard balance to strike, because on the one hand, ambitious climate targets "will serve to organize and measure the best of our skills and abilities" (J.F.K.); but on the other, it encourages *bad actors* to engage in activities that might be labelled by some as, "green-washing".

Some of those activities include the purchase of "bogus offsets" - which are typically cheap offsets that come from a dubious source. But we think that companies that get accused of buying these "bogus offsets" aren't doing it on purpose.

They're buying bogus offsets because there is fundamentally a huge gap between the supply of quality offsets and the demand for it. The demand side, is primarily driven by quick succession of bandwagoning climate commitments given by individuals, corporations, governments, and supranational organizations the world over.

The supply side is much trickier, since the science surrounding negative-emissions technology is so new. However, we think we have a solution that might mitigate the risk of companies buying "Bogus/Junk Offsets" altogether.

Using First Principles thinking to establish "limits" and begin with what we know to be true, we might say that:

Premise: Bogus offsets decrease confidence in carbon credit markets as a whole.

A) In extension, this also diminishes the efforts of organizations and government agencies attempting to reach ambitious climate targets.

B) If left untreated, bogus carbon offsets could severely cripple market confidence.

Conclusion: We need a solution that will clear away the fog of war currently shrouding the carbon offsets and 3-rd party certifications industries so as to edge out cheap, bogus offsets with high-quality offsets that have transparency built into the product architecture.

Description:

Each buoy produces 15 cubic meters per hour (about a third of a million liters daily), and multiple units can be added seamlessly to expand output. Designed for offshore mooring, the SW-15 minimizes land use, reduces costly civil works, and accelerates project start-up, ensuring a faster, lower-cost path to clean water. Its compact, container-sized design also allows relocation if community or industrial needs shift.

But scalability is only part of the story. The SW-15 is also efficient and environmentally sensitive by design. From anchoring to freshwater output, every system element reflects our commitment to sustainability. Unlike conventional land-based desalination plants, the SW-15 eliminates the need for brine disposal pipelines and their ongoing pumping costs, delivering significant operational savings. Its brine discharge occurs high above the sea floor, allowing natural dispersion and avoiding toxic pooling often linked to traditional desalination.

Equally important, our system avoids the transport and use of chemicals altogether. Filters are maintained with a simple backflush process, ensuring none enter the brine outflow. This innovative approach reduces operating costs, protects marine ecosystems, and provides a sustainable water solution you can invest in with confidence.

Name: Salient Direct Ocean Capture
Description: Salient Direct Ocean Capture (DOC) is developing electrochemical technology for carbon dioxide removal (CDR) from seawater. Their approach is designed for scalability and cost. The electrochemical approach uses only electricity and seawater as inputs, avoiding supply chain constraints on plant operations. It also employs the ocean as its carbon dioxide contactor, concentrating it to a hundred times that of the atmosphere by volume. Carbon dioxide removed from seawater can be sequestered through any durable storage mechanism and the effluent seawater returns to the ocean to remove more CO2 from the atmosphere. These efficiencies position Salient Direct Ocean Capture well to meet the projected need for 10-20 gigatons per year of global CDR capacity. Byproducts of the process can generate co-benefits and additional revenue streams to offset the cost of CDR and provide financial stability in nascent carbon removal markets.
